messages:
mira: Quick sync: noticed a customer report where a tenant enabled a heavy model via flag and instantly ate the quota for the whole pool. we need a failback for tenant-level quota saturation during rollouts.
tony: Yikes. They triggered >80% of GPU-minutes in 10m and blasted past their burst cap?
mira: Yup. They were in a gradual rollout but our per-route costs vary a lot and we didn't isolate tenant consumption.
ash: Proposal: `cohort_quota_policy` attached to a flag. semantics: evaluate per-cohort (tenant/tenant-group) usage and if a tenant exceeds cohort_quota_pct or absolute cap, automatically failback that tenant to a cheaper route variant.
mira: Minimal policy fields: `scope` (tenant|global), `cohort_selector`, `quota_pct_of_pool`, `absolute_quota_ms`, `failback_action` (route_to:MODEL|throttle|pause), `cooldown`, `notify` (email/pager), `audit_link`.
telemetry-bot: metric note: we already stream per-tenant gpu_ms and token counts. can reuse that. just need an alerting hook.
tonY: Implementation nuance: we must do evaluation atomically per-evaluation-window to avoid race where many tenants hit threshold simultaneously. maybe a leaky-bucket aggregator with priority ordering.
nash: Also edge-case: shared-tenants where billing is at org-level but tenants inside can spike. need to support `org_cohort` selector and tie to billing ids for enforcement.
sec: Security/privacy: console should never display other tenant ids unless user has access. when autopromoting failback, redact tenant names in global audit unless permitted.
console: UX ideas: show an inline "quota risk" indicator on the flag page. if any tenant is within X% of their configured quota, surface a yellow badge with a suggested action: reduce rollout speed or add per-tenant cap.
mira: API sketch: POST /v1/flags/{id}/cohort_quota_policy -> {"scope":"tenant","cohort_selector":"label:beta=true","quota_pct_of_pool":"5","absolute_quota_ms":"600000","failback_action":"route_to:stable-small","cooldown":"10m","notify":["#oncall","owner@company.com"],"audit_link":"..."}
tonY: When failback triggers, runtime should emit a ledger entry like: `failback:{policy_id, tenant_id(redacted), reason, window_ms, previous_route, new_route, owner}`. store for 90 days.
nash: We also want a graceful decay option: rather than full failback, step down weights for offending tenant: 100% -> 50% -> 0 across minutes. config param `decay_steps`.
telemetry-bot: Add a signal: `cohort_quota_headroom` which is 1 - (tenant_gpu_ms / allowed_ms) so dashboards can show heatmaps.
sec: Also require an approval if `failback_action=route_to` points to a model with different compliance boundary (e.g., private vs hosted).
nash: Good catch. Add `allowed_targets` whitelist to policy. runtime rejects policies with disallowed targets.
console: For the audit card, we can show anonymized tenant buckets and allow expanding when user has permission. also a "simulate" button to estimate which tenants would be affected given current telemetry.
mira: Who wants to own the RFC? I'll draft it with examples (cohort per-tenant, org-level, and label-based cohorts) and a sample migration to backfill policies.
tonY: I'll take runtime enforcement and leaky-bucket design.
nash: I'll do API + ledger format.
console: I'll prototype the UI mock and the simulate endpoint.
telemetry-bot: I'll add the `cohort_quota_headroom` metric export.
mira: Cool. I'll post the RFC here in ~24h. If anyone has immediate gotchas (multi-flag interactions, nested cohorts), drop them here. :raised_hands:
